bridge.title: Four things I noticed

beats.title: 100+ members, 10+ years of experience, and one price: $200 a month.
beats.text: Courses, daily breakdowns, live Q&A and group mentorship all sit inside the same monthly plan. A member who wants direct access to you has nothing to upgrade to.

beats.title: Your students post five- and six-figure wins. Your pricing is a monthly subscription.
beats.text: You already publish the proof: student results on your homepage, a social-proof wall, and a podcast episode with a student who got funded. That's the evidence a high-ticket tier is built on.

beats.title: Three of your pages send buyers to your DMs for a discount.
beats.text: The homepage, pricing page and results page all say “DM me for a discount”. That pushes your price down and pulls you into DMs. An application with a call works the other way around: people qualify themselves before you spend a minute.
beats.quote: “DM Me On Telegram For Instant Discount”

beats.title: “Won't a higher tier hurt the $200 group?” It sits on top of it.
beats.text: The group stays as it is. The mentorship is for the members going for a funded account who want someone to check their trades and their rule breaks. You already talk about exactly that: your newest video is about withdrawing, and your podcast features a funded student.

bridge.closing: So instead of explaining it, I built it. The page, the application, the emails and the ads, all below.

cards.title: You fail challenges on the rules, not the setups
cards.body: One oversized trade, one daily-drawdown breach, and the account is gone. The strategy was fine. The process wasn't.

cards.title: You learn alone
cards.body: Courses and videos teach the concepts. Nobody looks at your actual trades and tells you what you keep doing wrong.

cards.title: Passing isn't the finish line
cards.body: Getting funded is one step. Keeping the account and getting paid out needs the same discipline, every week.

mechanism.title: The Zapz Way
mechanism.body: No signals and no hype. You build one plan, follow fixed risk rules that match your prop firm's limits, execute it, and every week your trades get reviewed against that plan until the mistakes stop repeating.

preCallEmails.previewText: Your call with the ZapzTrading team is confirmed

Hey {{first_name}},

Your call is booked for {{call_time}}. The link is in your calendar invite.

Before we talk:
1. Keep the time free. We only hold a few mentorship calls each week.
2. Have your last 20 trades ready: a journal, screenshots or your challenge dashboard all work.

One note: payments for the mentorship never happen in DMs. Only through the official links from this email address.

preCallEmails.subject: Why most traders fail challenges on the rules
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Most failed challenges don't come from a bad setup. They come from one oversized position, one revenge trade, or one daily-drawdown breach.

That's why the mentorship starts with your rules, not a new strategy: risk per trade, max trades per day, and a stop when the day goes wrong.

On the call we'll look at where your process breaks today.

Team ZapzTrading

preCallEmails.subject: "I already have the $200 group. Why more?"
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

If you're in the ZapzTrading group, you already have the courses and the daily breakdowns. That doesn't change.

What the group can't do is look at your trades one by one and tell you which mistake you keep repeating. That's what the mentorship is for.

If you can fix that on your own, you don't need it, and we'll tell you so on the call.

Team ZapzTrading

preCallEmails.subject: What the call is (and isn't)
preCallEmails.previewText: No signals, no promises, just a straight conversation
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

So you know what to expect:

- The call takes about 30 minutes.
- We'll ask about your experience, your goal (challenge, funded account or personal account) and your risk rules.
- If the mentorship fits, we'll explain what's included and the investment.
- If it doesn't, we'll tell you and point you to the free resources.

What the call isn't: no signals, no trade calls, no promises of profits. Trading involves substantial risk.

Team ZapzTrading
